data.revised_prompt: The four diagonal arms and four circular motor mounts arranged in an X-shaped layout in <Picture 1> are <Subject 1>. The solid dark background and centered top-down framing in <Picture 1> are <Subject 2>. The target image transforms the flat schematic of <Subject 1> into a photorealistic 8K industrial design rendering of a matte black quadcopter with a faceted fuselage, carbon fiber components, and orange LED accents under soft overhead lighting. <Subject 1> is partially preserved; its exact positions, angles, scale, and proportions—corresponding to a 35cm rotor-to-rotor distance, a 1.3:1 arm span ratio, and a 52° rotor angle—are retained, while the flat grey shapes are replaced by three-dimensional foldable carbon fiber arms and reinforced motor covers. <Subject 2> is partially preserved; the 90-degree overhead viewpoint, framing, and dark backdrop remain, while the lighting changes to soft 5500K illumination casting high-contrast shadows. Replacing the flat geometry of <Subject 1>, the four arms are rendered as sleek, foldable exposed woven carbon fiber tubes connected to the central body via modular quick-release connectors and secured with exposed titanium fasteners. Each of the four terminal mounts becomes a machined, reinforced matte black motor cover with cooling vents. A newly designed faceted fuselage occupies the center where the arms intersect, featuring sharp 30-degree beveled edges, a curved upper shell with a 20cm wing curvature radius, a recessed anodized aluminum honeycomb grille on the front section, and a slim GPS antenna mast protruding from the top surface. Four two-blade carbon fiber propellers are mounted atop the motors at the ends of <Subject 1>, angled at 52 degrees relative to the airframe axes. Thin glowing orange LED light bands trace the leading edges of the fuselage and arms. Soft 5500K overhead lighting creates crisp specular highlights along the carbon weave, metallic fasteners, and anodized grille, while casting deep, high-contrast contact shadows across the matte black surfaces and onto <Subject 2>.
